statement: acme-sign 1.4.2 accepts the all-zero signature (r = 0, s = 0) for any message, so a forged signature would verify. Release 1.4.3 rejects it in every retest run so far.

statusHistory.note: Flagged as probable missing range check.
Relevant: forgery of a payment instruction would be accepted.
Protocol v1 results reviewed; recommendation rec-001 drafted.
Recommendation rec-001 approved for Acme to act on.

assumptions: The signing service calls verify() from acme_sign.ecdsa as described in intake answer iq-1.
Synthetic keys behave like production keys for this code path.
limitations: Only the verify() entry point was exercised; other entry points and the signing path were not.
Exploitability in Acme's deployed service depends on whether externally supplied signatures reach verify() (intake question iq-3 is open).
technicalDetail: ECDSA verification computes u1 = e * s^-1 and u2 = r * s^-1 mod n and checks that the x-coordinate of u1*G + u2*Q equals r mod n. Without the check 1 <= r, s <= n-1, the inputs r = 0 and s = 0 collapse the computation so that the comparison trivially succeeds (the exact failure path depends on how the implementation handles the zero inverse; in acme-sign 1.4.2 the modular inverse of 0 is computed as 0 and the point at infinity's x-coordinate is encoded as 0). Run #10 shows only r = 0 is affected in this implementation; s = 0 with in-range r is rejected by an unrelated code path. 1.4.3 adds the explicit range check before any field arithmetic. Background: the same class of missing-range-check bug was reported in 2022 as CVE-2022-21449 in a widely used Java runtime; acme-sign and this project are fictional.

statement: Run #5 measured a verification p99 of 2.60 ms against the 2.0 ms budget, but the run omitted the required warm-up. A compliant run (#6) measured 1.62 ms. Whether 1.4.2 has a latency regression is unresolved; two agents disagree and no deterministic check or reviewer has decided.

statusHistory.note: Conflict recorded between the triage agent's claim and the Autoresearcher's reading of run #6.

assumptions: The reference sandbox profile is representative enough to judge the budget (intake assumption iq-2).
limitations: Two runs only; no repeat across sandbox slots or times of day.
Only agent claims so far; the label stays Estimate until a check or reviewer decides.

between.claim: 1.4.2 has a latency regression: p99 2.60 ms in run #5.
Run #5 is a cold-start artifact; run #6 with warm-up is 1.62 ms.

conflicts.summary: The agents disagree about whether run #5 measures the library or the measurement setup. Agreement between agents could not settle this anyway; a repeat protocol is proposed.

technicalDetail: Run #5 used warmup_iterations=0, overriding the test definition default of 200. The first iterations include interpreter start-up, C-extension loading and CPU frequency ramp. Run #6 followed the definition and measured p99 1.62 ms. Proposal prop-latency-method would repeat the measurement five times across sandbox slots with and without warm-up to separate library latency from setup effects.

statement: The signing service configuration permits sha1 as a message digest. Acme reports that no production path selects it, but the permission remains and was not tested.

statusHistory.note: Judged unused in production paths per intake answers.
Relevant as configuration hygiene; not a demonstrated weakness.
Recommendation rec-002 drafted as general guidance.

assumptions: The imported configuration matches what is deployed.
limitations: No test exercised a sha1-digested signature; the finding is about permitted configuration, not observed behaviour.
technicalDetail: allowed_digests: [sha256, sha384, sha1] in the 2026-10 configuration. Removing sha1 is general guidance from current digest recommendations; this project did not measure any effect of leaving it in place.
